items.objective: Complete independent payload-declaration and exact-total-length guards.
items.prompt: Complete the queue validator after count and width have been checked. Header length is 7. Fill both blanks: if declared != ____: reject; if len(raw) != ____: reject.

feedback.a: Width counts bytes in one entry, while declared covers all entries. The actual file also includes the seven-byte header, so it cannot be compared with payload length alone.
feedback.b: Adding entry count to entry width mixes two quantities. Multiply to obtain payload bytes, then add the header bytes for total length.
feedback.c: Count times bytes per entry gives expected payload bytes. Header bytes plus declared payload bytes gives the exact total, catching both truncation and trailing data.

items.derivation: For count 2 and width 3, expected payload is 2*3=6 and total is 7+6=13. For count 0, expected payload is 0 and total is 7.

items.objective: Preserve unknown bytes while limiting semantic claims to the available evidence.
items.prompt: Two valid teaching queues differ only in the header unknown byte and the first entry's unknown byte. Both decoded readings stay the same. What can your inspector and format note justify?

choices.text: Delete both bytes from output because unchanged readings prove they are padding.
Retain the new raw hex bytes and report that these probes did not change the readings; their purpose remains unknown.
Name both bytes checksums because they can vary independently of the readings.

feedback.a: Unchanged readings only show that these reading calculations did not consume the changed bytes. It does not establish padding, and deletion violates the example's requirement to retain them.
feedback.b: The locations and raw values are observable. Preserving them keeps that evidence available, while the unchanged readings support only the narrower statement about these probes.
feedback.c: A checksum claim needs evidence relating the bytes to protected content. Independent variation and unchanged readings do not establish that rule; retain the bytes under their unknown names.

items.derivation: The declared reading slices exclude the unknown positions. Changing excluded bytes leaves those integer calculations unchanged. No declared rule assigns the unknown bytes a semantic role.

items.objective: Choose a malformed-input mutation that distinguishes an exact-size check from a minimum-size check.
items.prompt: Two queue inspectors agree on a valid one-entry file. A checks len(raw) >= 7 + declared; B checks equality. Both apply the same other guards and preserve unknowns. Which change to that valid file directly distinguishes this size-check difference?

choices.text: Append one byte without changing the header.
Change an unknown entry byte from 00 to 90.
Remove the last entry byte without changing the header.

feedback.a: A valid one-entry queue has 7+3=10 bytes. Appending one makes 11 while the declaration still requires 10. A's minimum-size check accepts it; B's equality check rejects it.
feedback.b: The length remains 10 and the declared format permits every unknown-byte value. Both checks still pass, so this tests preservation rather than the size-check difference.
feedback.c: The file becomes 9 bytes while 10 are required. Both the minimum-size and exact-size checks reject it. Truncation is useful to test, but it does not separate these two implementations.

items.derivation: Original length = 7+1*3 = 10. Appended length 11 satisfies 11>=10 but fails 11==10. A removed-byte length 9 fails both comparisons.

items.objective: Apply envelope validation and signed decoding while retaining an unfamiliar entry byte.
items.prompt: Apply the declared queue format to 51 54 01 03 03 00 00 ff fe d4. After validating the envelope, which result follows for its entry?

feedback.a: The envelope and unknown byte are right, but 65279 is the unsigned reading of ff fe. The field is signed and its top bit is set, so subtract 65536 to obtain -257.
feedback.b: ff is the first byte of the two-byte reading. The entry starts at offset 7, so its unknown byte is at offset 9: d4. Recompute positions before interpreting values.
feedback.c: Count 1 and width 3 require payload 3 and total 10, matching the bytes. The signed reading is 255+254*256-65536=-257. The remaining entry byte is retained as d4; the header's unknown byte is 00.

items.derivation: count=1; width=3; declared=3; total=7+3=10. Entry begins at 7. ff fe is 255+254*256=65279 unsigned, then 65279-65536=-257 signed. raw[9:10].hex() is d4.
